PullRequest.Title: Update Component Explorer packages
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- update Component Explorer, CLI, Vite plugin, and webpack plugin to the latest next releases
- pick up screenshot capture error reporting from microsoft/vscode-packages#287
- refresh the root, Vite, and Rspack lockfiles

## Validation

- verified installed package versions
- smoke-tested the updated CLI
- rendered sessions/remoteHostUnavailable/remoteHostUnavailableEmptyState/HostNotRunning/Dark successfully with an image hash and hasError=false

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The before/after lock metadata, parent optional-dependency fan-out, and CI critical path are directly visible. npm lockfile v3 uses these OS/CPU/libc fields to filter optional packages; with libc absent, both same-OS/same-CPU variants are eligible. Exact tarball sizes are unknown, which limits severity rather than mechanism confidence.
Findings.PerformanceResource: native-package tarball bytes, extracted files, and filesystem operations
Findings.PerformanceScaling: On a Linux x64 or arm64 install, each of three native package families now has two eligible same-OS/same-CPU artifacts instead of one; cold `npm ci` therefore grows from three matching binary artifacts to six, with one redundant GNU/musl variant per family.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased dependency-install latency, network transfer, disk usage, and extraction I/O on cache misses
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The base lockfile carried `libc: [glibc]` or `libc: [musl]` on the Linux variants for `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`, `@github/copilot`, and `@vscode/os-proxy-resolver`, so npm could exclude the incompatible variant before fetching and unpacking it.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: This lockfile refresh deletes every `libc` selector while retaining both GNU and musl packages as optional dependencies with identical Linux OS and CPU constraints, making both variants eligible in the lockfile's install tree.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: At deleted lines 255-257 the PR removes the first `libc: [glibc]` constraint; the same diff removes the paired musl/glibc constraints at old lines 272-274, 289-291, 306-308, 1218-1220, 1237-1239, 1256-1258, 1275-1277, and 4847-4911, without removing either optional package from its parent.
Findings.Title: Restore the libc filters for optional native binaries
Findings.Impact: A Linux x64 cache-miss `npm ci`—including the root install on component-fixtures and CSS-order-scan CI—downloads and unpacks both x64 variants for all three families before any build or fixture can start. Warm node_modules-cache hits avoid the install, but fresh developer/CI installs pay the extra binary transfer and disk cost.
Findings.Evidence: The parent entries enumerate GNU and musl optional dependencies for all three families (`package-lock.json` current lines 202-213, 1155-1164, and 4779-4788). After the deletion, each corresponding Linux package retains only `os: [linux]` and the same `cpu` value (for example current lines 246-295, 1199-1268, and 4820-4881), so npm's lockfile platform check can no longer distinguish libc. The component fixture workflows put `npm ci --ignore-scripts` on the cache-miss critical path before build/test (`.github/workflows/component-fixtures.yml:48-60` and `.github/workflows/css-order-scan.yml:39-51`).
Findings.Recommendation: Restore the deleted `libc` arrays (or regenerate the lockfile with the repository-supported npm version that preserves them) so only the host's GNU or musl artifact is fetched and unpacked.

Scenarios.Scenario: Fresh dependency installation for developer and CI component-fixture workflows
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The root `npm ci --ignore-scripts` must complete before build dependencies, Rspack compilation, Playwright installation, and fixture tests can progress; it is skipped only on a restored node_modules-cache hit.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: package-lock.json deleted libc selectors at old lines 255-308, 1218-1277, and 4847-4911
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch optional native-package tarballs from the npm registry
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Linux x64/arm64 changes from one matching artifact per family to both GNU and musl artifacts: 6 fetches rather than 3 across the three affected families.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The base lock's libc selectors excluded one variant per family before fetch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All eligible package fetches must settle before root `npm ci` completes and CI can build or test.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: package-lock.json optional package entries for Anthropic CLI, Copilot CLI, and OS proxy resolver
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Unpack and retain optional native binary packages in node_modules
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One redundant extracted package per family on Linux, adding 3 package trees on x64/arm64.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only the host-libc package was eligible for extraction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Extraction runs during awaited `npm ci`; retained files also enlarge node_modules and its saved cache.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Optional native-package families applicable to the host. On Linux x64/arm64, three families each expose GNU and musl variants; effective cardinality changes from 3 selected native artifacts to 6 eligible artifacts.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The workflow serializes root, build, and Rspack `npm ci` steps. npm may fetch packages concurrently internally, but the job awaits all root fetch/extract work before proceeding, so added fan-out remains on the critical path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A node_modules-cache hit skips the affected root install in the fixture workflows. On a miss, a warm npm content cache can reduce network transfer but both variants remain eligible for extraction and retained disk space; a cold npm cache downloads all eligible tarballs.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: parent optional-dependency sets, removed lock selectors, matching remaining OS/CPU constraints, and awaited CI install paths are directly evidenced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Tarball byte sizes and npm registry-cache hit rates are not present in the repository, so exact seconds and megabytes are uncertain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity boundary fan-out: the diff removes the only metadata that separates GNU and musl variants during lockfile platform selection.

Scenarios.Scenario: Start or statically build the Component Explorer through Rspack or Vite
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The single Rspack/Vite process must discover fixture modules and compile the explorer before the dev server is ready or the static artifact can be uploaded.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Glob `src/**/*.fixture.ts`, read modules/assets, and write the Rspack/Vite bundle
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One repository-wide fixture discovery per build/server startup, followed by reads proportional to matched fixtures and their module graph.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same plugin options, include glob, and bundler startup path existed before; only package versions changed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Discovery and initial compilation gate server readiness/static artifact production.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One bundler process per serve/build invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same commands and process count existed before the version bump.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The process must become ready or finish before fixture rendering/testing continues.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number of files matching `src/**/*.fixture.ts` plus their transitive source/assets; one plugin instance serves the whole repository fixture set.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One build/dev-server process is launched per workflow or developer command. Internal bundler parallelism is unchanged by the visible configuration; there is no new queue, burst, or per-fixture subprocess in the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A static Rspack build cleans its output and recompiles; a running dev server can use normal incremental module state. node_modules is cached separately in CI. The dependency version bump does not visibly change cache keys or add a cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the unchanged call path and boundary cardinality; insufficient evidence of any version-induced regression mechanism.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The updated packages' internal source is not in the supplied diff, so internal timing changes cannot be established from names or versions alone.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: manifests update package versions, but the diff does not show added scans, increased cardinality, defeated caching, or new critical-path boundaries.

Scenarios.Scenario: Serve and render fixture screenshots, including CSS-order scans and bisection
Scenarios.CriticalPath: `component-explorer serve` launches the Rspack server and waits for readiness; each `render` invocation then launches a Node CLI process, navigates a browser against the local server, and writes images/manifest before the caller can inspect results.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launch the Component Explorer CLI for each render probe
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two full-set renders plus about 2*ceil(log2(D)) probes for each order-dependent fixture; all are sequential.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same per-render child-process launch and sequential probe structure existed before.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Every child process and browser render is awaited by the scan/bisection.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Navigate/render against the localhost Component Explorer server
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One local browser-render interaction per CLI render invocation; the same server is reused.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same localhost server and render path existed before.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each render must receive and capture the fixture before its manifest is consumed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write screenshot images/manifests and read/copy scan outputs
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Output scales with rendered fixtures plus two copied images per detected candidate; probe directories scale with render invocation count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Output directories, manifests, hash-path behavior, and report copies were unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Manifest reads are awaited per render and report writes gate scan completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: For a normal scan, two render invocations cover all F matching fixtures, then each of C changed fixtures performs two sequential binary searches over D stylesheet documents, totaling approximately 2 + O(C log D) CLI/browser invocations.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The CSS-order scanner awaits baseline and reversed renders serially and processes candidates in a serial loop; each bisection probe awaits the previous probe. The already-running serve is reused, with no diff-introduced concurrency burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The serve/module graph is warm and reused across probes. Render outputs use separate directories; hash paths deduplicate identical image names within output behavior, but there is no cross-invocation result cache. None of these cache semantics is changed by the visible diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for subprocess/filesystem/local-network reachability and serialized multiplicity; no visible evidence that the bump increases any of them.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The new CLI package implementation and screenshot error-reporting change are external to the supplied diff, so no claim can be made about their internal CPU, browser, or I/O cost.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the package bump reaches a hot scaling workflow, but version metadata alone does not prove more work, retention, or boundary calls.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all six changed files and every diff page. One concrete regression was reported: deleted libc selectors double eligible GNU/musl native artifacts across three package families on Linux cache-miss installs. The Rspack/Vite build and CLI screenshot paths retain their prior visible boundary counts and scheduling, with no other diff-proven regression.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
